# Build sequence and evidence gates

2 October 2026. Owners below are proposed roles, not assigned people. Calendar deadline UNKNOWN; schedule depends on supplier drawings and workshop access.

Execution basis updated 3 October: college/NGO funding only. No college lab, workshop or faculty support assumed. Assistant prepares design/calculations/software; ENTC review optional/unconfirmed. Required physical services are bought/rented/hired. See [no-lab route](NO_LAB_BUILD_ROUTE.md).

## Fastest responsible sequence

| Gate | Work | Output and condition to proceed | Owner role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1: basis | Measure test room; agree particle target airflow/noise and duty hours; define outdoor research goal | Approved one-page requirements; no claimed outdoor radius | User/team with assistant preparation and scoped review |
| 2: suppliers | Obtain fan/filter drawings and clean/loaded curves; compare fans at actual duty | Exact parts and complete pressure budget; quotations, not purchases | Assistant comparisons + team + suppliers |
| 3: design | Physical CAD assembly, seals, structural calculations, electrical drawings, manufacturing BOM | Mechanical and electrical review; drawing revisions frozen | Assistant preparation + qualified reviewers + fabricator/electrical assembler |
| 4: fit | Inspect incoming parts; frame/filters/ducts dry assembly | Fits service envelopes; no unexplained bypass; guards installed | Fabricator + team |
| 5: commissioning | Electrical checks and guarded first run | Qualified electrical acceptance; stable operation; no unsafe vibration/heat | Electrician + mechanical mentor |
| 6: indoor evidence | Airflow pressure power noise seal and room particle tests | Repeatable documented findings; no invented certified CADR | Team + test mentor |
| 7: outdoor redesign | Weather structure public-access protection; map real wind/site | Separate outdoor mechanical/electrical approval | Assistant preparation + relevant qualified reviewers/site owner |
| 8: outdoor pilot | One unit first; controls and repeated spatial measurements | Evidence of useful local benefit, maintenance and energy cost | Team + site mentor |
| 9: network | Test a second unit only after useful single-unit evidence | Determine spacing from measurements, not drawn circles | Team + stakeholders |

Start supplier requests, room measurements, CAD packaging and mentor reviews in parallel. Do not wait for formaldehyde research to test a particulate-only tower. Do not pay for a custom PCB or solar system before the core fan/filter assembly works.

## Indoor test plan

1. Record room volume, windows/doors, ventilation state, background particles, occupancy restrictions and sensor calibration. No toxic gas, smoke or deliberately harmful aerosol challenge in occupied space.
2. Measure actual airflow with an appropriate calibrated method, pressure at each stage, fan setting, power, sound at stated locations and temperatures. State instrument uncertainty and method. Free-air fan data is not measured assembled flow.
3. Inspect door/frame leakage; formal installed-filter certification requires a suitable professional procedure, not consumer sensors.
4. Compare particle decay with tower off and on under matched conditions; repeat at least three paired trials as a provisional research plan. Use multiple room locations and record humidity. Sensor co-location before/after checks for drift; low particle counts may make the test inconclusive.
5. If well-mixed decay fits are justified, estimate CADR = room volume x (on decay rate - off decay rate), with rates in inverse hours; report uncertainty and ventilation differences. This is an experimental estimate, not AHAM certification. A positive result without uncertainty/control is insufficient.
6. Evaluate a supplier-approved safe restriction/loading scenario, not dust dumping. Check required minimum airflow and thermal behaviour. Do not deliberately block the fan beyond OEM limits.

Acceptance numbers must be approved at Gate 1: minimum actual airflow, acceptable noise at stated distance, duty duration and maintenance criteria. Electrical/guarding failures mean stop irrespective of airflow. A particle reduction claim requires matched controls and repeatable improvement above measurement uncertainty.

## Outdoor measurements before a bubble claim

Record wind speed/direction and background particles simultaneously, with an upwind control and breathing-height points at proposed distances in several directions. Alternate tower on/off over repeated comparable periods and evaluate confidence intervals, sensor drift and changing sources. Measure fan exhaust and intake recirculation. Indoor decay formula cannot be used to certify an outdoor radius.

Draw circles only as proposed measurement zones, not promised clean-air boundaries. Two units may interact; their effects are not necessarily additive. Stop scaling if the pilot cannot show useful benefit versus background variability.

## Upcoming work window (not a promised deadline)

First: room survey, target agreement, OEM data requests, mentor access. Then: physical assembly CAD and loss budget, supplier quotes, electrical/structural review. Only after release: procurement, fabrication and commissioning. End with indoor evidence report and decision whether outdoor pilot is justified. Track dates and owners once people and supplier lead times are known.
